title: Give exact change from a coin till
instruction: The customer is owed 35 cents. Take exactly 35 cents from the till and put it in the change tray.
context: Counting out change is a routine cashier step: the cashier maps an amount to coins of different sizes and values, picks thin coins out of a till and hands over exactly that amount. Two coin sets make 35 cents with the coins on hand (a quarter and a dime, or a quarter and two nickels), while taking one coin of each kind gives 40 cents and overpays, so the policy has to use the stated amount, not a fixed habit. Done by: cashiers and retail salespersons.
setup: On the table in front of the left arm (x forward from the arm bases, y left). Positions are table coordinates in metres, origin on the base line at the midline; the left arm's base is at (0, 0.305), 305 mm left of the midline, and the table top is z = 0.7475 m. Every object is a rigid matte primitive with one friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Fixed: a coin till, an open-topped box of 5 mm walls 15 mm tall, its outline running from x = 0.140 to 0.310 and from y = 0.2075 to 0.4025 (dark grey, sRGB 0.18, 0.18, 0.20). Two dividers (5 mm thick, 15 mm tall, running along y) split it into three compartments, each 50 mm along x and 180 mm along y inside, centred at x = 0.170 (nickels), 0.225 (quarters) and 0.280 (dimes), y = 0.305; the table is their floor. A change tray, an open-topped box of 5 mm walls 15 mm tall, 100 x 100 mm inside, centred at (0.225, 0.110) (grey, sRGB 0.30, 0.30, 0.34); the table is its floor. Loose: six US coins lying flat (one face up), at US Mint dimensions and masses: two nickels (21.21 mm across, 1.95 mm thick, 5.000 g, sRGB 0.70, 0.71, 0.72), two quarters (24.26 mm, 1.75 mm, 5.670 g, sRGB 0.76, 0.77, 0.78) and two dimes (17.91 mm, 1.35 mm, 2.268 g, sRGB 0.78, 0.79, 0.80). Each compartment holds its two coins on its centre line along y, at y = 0.345 and y = 0.265 (80 mm apart, 52.5 mm from the compartment's long walls). The right arm is idle at its ready pose. To build it: cut the till and tray walls from 5 mm acrylic or wood (or print them) and glue them to a board taped to the table at the stated positions; use real US coins.
scoring: End state only, judged after the arms stop from a top photo and a tape measure. Each coin is in exactly one place: in the tray if its centre lies over the tray's 100 x 100 mm inner floor and its lowest point is below the 15 mm rim; in the till if its centre lies over any compartment's 50 x 180 mm inner floor and its lowest point is below the 15 mm rim; otherwise loose (on the counter, on a wall top, held above a rim, off the table). A coin counts whatever its face, tilt or stacking once it is in the tray. Add up the coins in the tray (nickel 5, dime 10, quarter 25 cents). Over 35 cents: 0. Exactly 35 cents with no coin loose: 1.0. Exactly 35 cents with one or more coins loose: 0.75. Under 35 cents: 0.5 x (cents in the tray) / 35, which is 0 for an empty tray, 0.14 at 10 cents, 0.36 at 25 cents and 0.43 at 30 cents. Success, which ends the trial, is exactly 35 cents in the tray with no coin loose and every coin at rest (under 10 mm/s and 0.5 rad/s), held for 1 s. The full-score sets are a quarter and a dime, or a quarter and two nickels; coins moved from one till compartment to another are still in the till. In simulation each coin's lowest point is computed from its centre, axis and size, and a centre exactly on the inner floor's edge counts (0.1 mm epsilon). The till and tray are fixed in simulation; on the real rig, a trial in which either moves more than 5 mm from its mark scores 0. The scorer reads object poses, not the gripper: in simulation a coin held below the tray rim would count; on real arms the photo after the arm parks decides.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Lay the six coins back flat at their marks in the till compartments. Run with -E object_jitter=0: the layout and the open-loop demo depend on it.
fidelity: Approximate: the coins are plain cylinders at US Mint diameter, thickness and mass, with no rims, reeding or relief, and the same rubber-like friction as everything else (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), more than metal on metal. The coins lie spaced out, two per compartment, rather than piled in deep till cups, so a parallel gripper can reach a coin's rim; the till is shallow (15 mm) and has no drawer or cash slots. The tray is a fixed open box. No customer is simulated.
